subject: Status page: transient duplicate responses & automatic routing fallback (hosted API)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@jupiterhealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Status page: transient duplicate responses & automatic routing fallback (hosted API)

Hi Aisha —

Quick heads-up: we’ve posted a short status advisory for a transient issue that affected a subset of hosted API requests in us-west earlier this morning. Symptoms you may have seen: occasional duplicate completions for single requests and a small number of 502/503 responses while our routing layer performed an automatic fallback.

What we know right now:
- Time window: 08:40–09:05 PT (approx).
- Impact: ~0.7% of requests for affected model routes experienced duplicate generations; ~0.2% returned a 502/503 before being retried by the client or our gateway.
- Root trigger (initial): routing reconciliation between two regional edge proxies caused a transient request replay.

Immediate mitigation: our routing layer disabled the reconciler, and we reverted the quick routing change at 09:01 PT — traffic returned to normal and duplicates dropped to baseline. Engineering is continuing a detailed investigation.

We’re tracking this on the status page: https://status.redwood.inference/incidents/2027-12-09-routing-fallback (short summary + timeline). I’ve attached a short log excerpt that shows the duplicate-response fingerprints we observed (jupiter_health_response_log.txt).

Next steps from our side:
- Postmortem with timeline + customer-facing summary (ETA: EOD tomorrow).
- Mitigation guidance if you want to reduce the chance of duplicates reaching your application (small SDK/HTTP retry pattern notes).

If you saw anything larger in your telemetry (higher error rate, customer impact), please send the logs and we’ll prioritize.

Appreciate the patience — I’ll keep you updated as we have the follow-up.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake | Strategic Accounts (Hosted)
Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@jupiterhealth.com>

Date: Thu, 9 Dec 2027 09:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Status page: transient duplicate responses & automatic routing fallback (hosted API)

Thanks for the heads-up, Jordan. We did see a spike in duplicate completions in our production logs between 08:44–08:55 PT for the /v1/generate route. The duplicates caused a few downstream records to be created twice (we’ve debounced in our service for now).

Can you confirm whether the duplicate content was identical payloads retried, or slightly different variations? Also, any immediate guidance on whether we should temporarily alter our retry/backoff to avoid reprocessing duplicate responses while you do the postmortem?

I attached a short excerpt from our SRE team’s logs in case that helps (we’ll share full logs if you need them).

— Aisha
Aisha Khan | Head of Integrations
Jupiter Health

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Dec 2027 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Status page: transient duplicate responses & automatic routing fallback (hosted API)

Jordan/Aisha — copying the quick internal triage notes so we can coordinate customer comms.

Summary (ops):
- Root cause: a reconciliation race between edge proxy A and edge proxy B during an incremental routing policy rollout. Under load, a small subset of in-flight requests were replayed while the proxies re-synced sticky session state. That replay manifested as duplicate completions.
- Duplicate content: mostly identical payloads (same prompt + same model seed), occasionally two completions produced micro-differences when tokens were generated in different worker instances.
- 09:01 PT: we disabled the reconciler and halted the rollout; replay rate dropped to near zero.
- Immediate mitigation applied: additional dedup headers injected at the gateway (idempotency token enforcement) and a temporary stricter routing policy for us-west.

Recommended customer-facing guidance (for Jordan):
1) Short-term SDK guidance: if you detect a 502/503 then use exponential backoff before retrying; for non-error duplicate content, apply an idempotency check using your request id to avoid double-processing.
2) We’ll publish a mitigation runbook (PDF) with exact header names and example client code.
3) Postmortem timeline: initial report EOD tomorrow, full postmortem and planned remedial changes within 7 business days.

I’ll attach the mitigation runbook draft once legal/product OKs the wording.

— Sean
Sean Gallagher | SRE
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Khan <aisha.k@jupiterhealth.com>, Jupiter Health SRE <sre@jupiterhealth.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2027 15:40:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up & customer summary — 2027-12-09 routing fallback incident

Hi Aisha —

Thanks again for the quick signal and logs; that helped speed the root cause work. Below is a concise customer-facing summary and next steps (we’re keeping it short so you can share with engineering/ops). If you’d like a longer write-up for your internal postmortem, let me know and we’ll send it.

What happened (summary):
- Between 08:40–09:05 PT on 2027-12-09, a partial routing policy rollout caused session-state reconciliation between two edge proxies. During that reconciliation, a small percentage of in-flight requests were replayed which produced duplicate completions. A tiny fraction of requests briefly returned 502/503 while the system retried.

Scope & impact:
- Affected route: hosted API /v1/generate for models: rwinf-small, rwinf-medium (customer-specific traffic shape concentrated on rwinf-medium).
- Customer impact: Jupiter Health observed duplicate completions for ~0.7% of requests during the window; we understand you saw downstream duplicate records.

Root cause:
- Logic in the edge reconciler allowed in-flight requests to be replayed during state synchronization under a specific timing window. The reconciliation logic assumed idempotent upstream behavior which the router did not fully guarantee in this edge-case.

Fixes implemented so far: 
- Reconciler rollback (09:01 PT) and rollback of the routing policy.
- Gateway idempotency header enforcement for new requests to block replays.
- Temporary tightening of routing consistency checks in us-west.

Planned permanent changes (timeline):
- Remedial change to reconciler: add explicit handshake and backpressure gating (ETA: 7 business days for rollout).
- Add end-to-end idempotency tokens in SDKs (ETA: 14 business days) + example code.
- Full postmortem (with logs, timeline, and regression tests) to be published by 2027-12-16.

Attachments: mitigation_runbook.pdf (example headers, sample client code, and quick checklist). Full logs excerpt: jupiter_health_response_log.txt.

Credits & next steps:
- We’d like to offer a service credit for the affected token usage window; I’ll coordinate CS to calculate that and send a formal credit memo.
- If you want a short live run-through of the mitigation runbook with your SREs, I can set up a 30-minute session early next week.

Again, apologies for the disruption. We’re treating this with high priority and will share the full postmortem on 2027-12-16.

Best,
— Jordan
Jordan Blake | Strategic Accounts (Hosted)
Redwood Inference
